newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian postmen deny they becoming police spies.
newsitem.headline: Belgian postmen deny they becoming police spies.

text.p: Belgian postal service chiefs denied on Thursday a report that postmen would act as spies for the police.
A police official told BRTN radio earlier in the day that postmen were already being used as informers in four towns in a pilot scheme that could spread.

"This sort of work is certainly not in the contract we have had for a long time with the government," the postal service chiefs said in a statement. "The management committee foresees no work of this type in the future."
But the police official said: "The idea is that...people who are out there in the streets professionally notify police when they see anything suspicious."
"We are extra eyes, extra ears, because postmen go everywhere," said a post office official in the town of Tienen.
A shocking child sex and murder scandal, dubbed the Dutroux case after chief suspect Marc Dutroux, has prompted floods of denunciations in the past three months.

The organisation of prominent child rights activist Marie-France Botte daily receives hundreds of letters containing denunciations, as do similar groups. A special hot line set up by police has taken thousands of calls.
